Day in Our Data · Saturday, October 3, 2026, 11 a.m. to 3 p.m.

Get started with AI coding

Never used an AI coding tool? Start here. Pick a path, get a working setup in about 15 minutes, and spend the rest of the day on Oak Park's data.

On this page

  1. Before you arrive
  2. Pick your path
  3. Path 1: the Civic Spark workspace
  4. Path 2: Claude on the web or desktop
  5. Path 3: install Claude Code on your laptop
  6. Your first 15 minutes
  7. Ground rules for AI tools today

Before you arrive

None of this is required. Each item saves you ten minutes at your table.

  • Charge your laptop and bring the charger. A tablet works for the browser workspace, but a keyboard helps.
  • Make a free GitHub account. You will want somewhere to save your project and link it from your showcase entry.
  • Skim the 15 starter projects and pick two you would enjoy.
  • Optional: install Claude Code (below) at home, where the Wi-Fi is not shared with 40 other people.

Free credits for today

Anthropic donated Claude credits for today. Pick up your credit link at the check-in table. It is not posted online, so keep it to yourself.

Pick your path

All three paths run the same kind of AI coding agent. They differ in how much you install. If you are not sure, take path 1.

Path 1 · Zero install · Recommended

The Civic Spark browser workspace

A ready-made coding environment built for this event. It runs in your browser, all the starter projects are already loaded, and you cannot break anything. It has an Agent tab for chatting with the AI and a Terminal tab for typing commands.

Set up path 1

Path 2 · No terminal

Claude on the web or the desktop app

Use Claude Code at claude.ai/code in the browser, or in the Code tab of the Claude desktop app. Good if you already have a Claude account and want a point-and-click window.

Set up path 2

Path 3 · Full power

Install Claude Code on your laptop

Run Claude Code in your own terminal or code editor, on your own files. It takes the most setup and gives the most control. Your project stays on your machine after today.

Set up path 3

Path 1: the Civic Spark workspace

  1. Open the workspace and sign in

    Go to https://test-site-civic-spark.fly.dev/ and create an account with any email address you can check.

  2. Enter your key before you start a session

    Open the Agent tab and paste your key first. If you start a session before entering a key, the agent has nothing to run on. Your table host hands you the GLM key at check-in.

    For GLM, paste the event key. For Claude, paste your own Claude token and pick Opus as the model.

  3. Say hello to the agent

    Type a plain-English request in the Agent tab. Try: List the starter projects in this workspace and tell me which one a beginner could finish in two hours.

  4. Optional: use the terminal instead

    Prefer typing commands? In the Terminal tab, run opencode for the GLM agent, or claude for Claude Code after you have entered your Claude token.

You cannot break it

The workspace is disposable by design. Try things, ask the agent to undo things, start over. If something looks wrong, a table host can reset it.

Path 2: Claude on the web or desktop

  1. Sign in with a Claude account that includes Claude Code

    Claude Code needs a Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise, or Console account. The free claude.ai plan does not include it. The event credits apply to a Console account: see the check-in table.

  2. Open Claude Code

    On the web, go to claude.ai/code and connect your GitHub account when asked. In the desktop app, open the Code tab.

  3. Point it at the event repository

    Choose or fork https://github.com/oak-park-cisc/Oak_Park_Day_in_our_Data so the starter projects and cached data are right there.

  4. Ask your first question

    Try: Read the starter project cards and the data catalog, then suggest three maps or charts I could finish today.

Path 3: install Claude Code on your laptop

Claude Code runs on macOS 13+, Windows 10 (1809) or later, and most Linux distributions, with 4 GB of memory or more. You do not need administrator rights.

  1. Open a terminal

    Mac: press Cmd+Space, type Terminal, press Enter. Windows: press the Windows key, type PowerShell, press Enter. Linux: you know where it is.

  2. Run the installer for your system

    Copy the one line for your system, paste it into the terminal, press Enter.

    Windows: installing Git for Windows is optional but lets Claude Code use Git Bash. If you see 'irm' is not recognized, you are in CMD, not PowerShell.

  3. Check it worked

    Close the terminal, open a new one, and run the version check. If it says claude is not found, open a fresh terminal once more, then ask a table host.

  4. Get the event data and start Claude

    Download the event repository, move into it, and start Claude Code. The first run opens your browser to sign in.

    No git? Download the repository as a ZIP from GitHub (green Code button, then Download ZIP), unzip it, and cd into the folder.

  5. Optional: use it inside your editor

    Install the Claude Code extension for VS Code (it also works in Cursor), or the plugin for JetBrains IDEs. See where to code for the trade-offs.

Your first 15 minutes

Same steps on every path. Type these into the agent in plain English. You do not need to know any code.

  1. Let it read the project

    Run /init. Claude reads the files and writes a CLAUDE.md: notes it will reread at the start of every session.

  2. Ask for a tour

    Explain what is in this repository like I have never coded before. What data is here and what could I make with it?

  3. Plan before you build

    Press Shift+Tab until the mode shows plan. Claude now researches and proposes a plan without changing any files. Say Plan a simple map for starter project 11 (the urban forest). Read the plan, push back, then switch out of plan mode and say Go.

  4. See it running

    Show me how to open what you just built. Claude will give you a command, a file to open, or a link.

  5. Save your work

    Commit this with a clear message and help me push it to a new GitHub repository. You will paste that link into your showcase entry.

Stuck? Say so

Paste the error message and ask What does this mean and how do I fix it? Press Esc to stop Claude mid-task. Press Esc twice to rewind to an earlier point.

Ground rules for AI tools today

  • Keys and tokens are passwords. Never paste one into a file you commit, a public chat, a screenshot, or your showcase entry. If one leaks, tell a table host so it can be revoked.
  • Public data only. Do not give the AI confidential or personal information.
  • Check what the AI tells you. Open the chart, read the numbers, ask How do you know that? Label prototypes as prototypes.
  • Record your sources. Ask Claude to write the data sources into your README as it works.
  • Nothing made today is an official Village product or position.
